# Graphs in Competitive Programming

> This repo is a study path for graph algorithms from the absolute basics up to roughly Codeforces 1800 level.

- [Graphs in Competitive Programming](https://docs.example.com/readme.md): Graphs in Competitive Programming
- [01 Basics](https://docs.example.com/01-basics/readme.md): Target range: roughly 800-1100
- [02 Core Patterns](https://docs.example.com/02-core-patterns/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1000-1300
- [03 Trees](https://docs.example.com/03-trees/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1200-1500
- [04 Shortest Paths](https://docs.example.com/04-shortest-paths/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1300-1700
- [05 DSU and MST](https://docs.example.com/05-dsu-and-mst/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1400-1700
- [06 Directed Graphs](https://docs.example.com/06-directed-graphs/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1500-1800
- [07 Advanced Connectivity](https://docs.example.com/07-advanced-connectivity/readme.md): Target range: roughly 1700-1800
- [00. TF is a graph?](https://docs.example.com/00-introduction/readme.md): In competitive programming, graphs are just a way to represent connections. We have nodes (things) and edges (relationships between those things).

- [1. Graph Representation](https://docs.example.com/01-basics/01-graph-representation.md): Difficulty band: 800-1000
- [2. Breadth First Search](https://docs.example.com/01-basics/02-bfs.md): Difficulty band: 800-1100
- [3. Depth First Search](https://docs.example.com/01-basics/03-dfs.md): Difficulty band: 800-1100
